ODC1.claim: Cuttack (Kataka), the Silver City, has over a thousand years of history — Barabati Fort, silver filigree, and dahi bara aloodum.

places.name: Cuttack (Kataka)
places.summary: Odisha's thousand-year-old Silver City — Barabati Fort, silver filigree and dahi bara aloodum.
places.seoDescription: Cuttack (Kataka): Barabati Fort, silver filigree, the Maritime Museum and Netaji's birthplace museum; best November–March, a day trip from Bhubaneswar.

overview.text:
Cuttack — Kataka in Odia — is a city shaped by more than a thousand years of history, and Odisha's Silver City. Its story runs from the ramparts of Barabati Fort to the fine silver filigree its workshops still turn out, and its favourite street food is dahi bara aloodum.

A day covers the highlights: the Odisha State Maritime Museum, the house where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born, the filigree workshops, the Museum of Justice and the old Killa Dalijoda, with the Ansupa nature camp further out.

how_to_reach.text: Kataka Railway Station serves the city; the nearest airport is Biju Patnaik International in Bhubaneswar, and regular buses, trains and taxis link the two cities.

local_transport.text: Mo Bus runs air-conditioned buses between Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Puri; app cabs such as Odisha Yatri, Ola and Rapido, taxis and autos cover the city.

places.summary: A quiet old port town on the Bay of Bengal — golden sands, a lighthouse and fresh seafood.
places.seoDescription: Gopalpur: a former colonial port in Ganjam with a lighthouse and golden beach; Panthanivas Gopalpur, Tampara Lake and Tara Tarini nearby; best October–February.

overview.text:
Gopalpur, in Ganjam district, is one of Odisha's most peaceful beaches. It was once a busy colonial port, and its old lighthouse and the fishing boats drawn up on the sand still hint at that past.

Today it is a place for slow days: golden sand, gentle waves, sunset walks and fresh seafood, with Tampara Lake, the Tara Tarini hill temple and the Blue Flag beach at Sonapur all within an hour or so.

how_to_reach.text: Take a train to Brahmapur and drive to the coast; the nearest airport is Biju Patnaik International in Bhubaneswar.

places.name: Chandipur
places.summary: The 'vanishing sea' beach of Baleshwar, where the tide retreats up to 5 km.
places.seoDescription: Chandipur: the sea recedes 3–5 km at low tide, so you can walk the seabed; Panthanivas on the beach; Baleshwar station; best October–March.

overview.text:
Chandipur, in Baleshwar district, is famous for one thing: its vanishing sea. At low tide the water pulls back as much as 3–5 km, leaving rippled sand, shallow pools, red crabs and shells, and you can walk far out across the seabed. When the tide returns, it is a quiet, uncrowded beach for sunrises and sunsets.

Kuldiha Wildlife Sanctuary and the Panchalingeswar temple are about half an hour away.

places.name: Similipal National Park
places.summary: Odisha's largest reserve — black tigers, sal forests and the Barehipani and Joranda waterfalls.
places.seoTitle: Similipal National Park and Tiger Reserve
places.seoDescription: Similipal: 2,750 sq km tiger reserve and UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, black tigers, Barehipani and Joranda falls; open 6 am–6 pm, best November–June.

overview.text:
Similipal Tiger Reserve spreads across 2,750 sq km of Mayurbhanj — Odisha's largest protected area, a Project Tiger reserve and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Plateaus, sal forest and river valleys rise to peaks over 1,500 m, and it is famous worldwide for its rare melanistic (black) tigers, along with elephants, gaur, leopards and more than 300 bird species.

The Barehipani and Joranda waterfalls are at their best after the monsoon. Baripada is the base town.

best_time.text: November to June; the waterfalls are fullest just after the monsoon.

how_to_reach.text: Baleshwar is the nearest railway station, about 60 km from Baripada; Bhubaneswar airport is about 250 km away. The park is reached by road from Baripada.

where_to_stay.text: OTDC's Panthanivas Baripada, near Similipal, is the recommended base.

overview.text:
Satkosia Tiger Reserve spans Anugola and Nayagada districts and takes its name from the 22 km gorge the Mahanadi carves through the Eastern Ghats ('satkosia' means seven kos). Forested hills and deep valleys shelter elephants, leopards, sambar and rich birdlife, and the river is a protected home for gharials and mugger crocodiles.

Stay in the eco-camps at Tikarpada, Chhotkei or Baghamunda for river boating, jungle safaris, birdwatching and guided walks.

best_time.text: November to March. Closed every Tuesday.

places.summary: The 'Kashmir of Odisha' — pine forests, coffee gardens and cool winters in Kandhamala.
places.seoDescription: Daringbadi: a cool hill station in Kandhamala with pine forests, coffee gardens and near-freezing winter nights; best October–February, via Phulbani.

overview.text:
Daringbadi, high in Kandhamala, is fondly called the 'Kashmir of Odisha'. Pine forests, coffee plantations, waterfalls and misty valleys surround it, and winter nights can dip close to freezing — a rarity in Odisha.

The hills grow organic turmeric, spices and coffee, and the coffee garden is just 3 km from town; Mandasaru valley and Midhubandha waterfall are further out.

best_time.text: October to February; winter nights can be close to freezing.

how_to_reach.text: Take a train to Brahmapur and drive via Phulbani. Bhubaneswar airport is about 210 km from Phulbani.

where_to_stay.text: An eco nature camp is the preferred option; Phulbani has hotels and guest houses.

overview.text:
Koraput is Odisha's southern highland: rolling hills, deep valleys, coffee plantations, Kotpad handloom and a rich tribal culture. Deomali, at about 1,672 m, is the state's highest peak, and the Machkund river plunges about 157 m at Duduma falls on the Andhra border.

Give it three days: sunsets over Kolab reservoir, the Putsil valley, the Gupteswar cave temple and the weekly tribal haats.

how_to_reach.text: Visakhapatnam is the nearest major airport, about 170 km away. By rail, Jayapur station is about 22 km and Koraput Junction about 30 km.

where_to_stay.text: OTDC's Deomali Nature Camp is the preferred stay; there is also a Panthanivas in Jeypore, and hotels in Koraput town.

overview.text:
Sambalpur is western Odisha's cultural hub on the Mahanadi. The 16th-century Samaleswari Temple anchors the city, Sambalpuri handloom fills its markets, and its folk music and dance are known across the state.

Hirakud Dam, the Leaning Temple of Huma, the Kardola weavers' village and safaris at Debrigarh are all within reach — give it two days.

places.seoDescription: Hirakud Dam: over 25 km across the Mahanadi near Sambalpur, Gandhi and Jawahar Minar viewpoints, winter birds; open 6 am–6 pm, free.

overview.text:
Hirakud Dam stretches more than 25 km across the Mahanadi near Sambalpur — one of the longest earthen dams in the world. Built in the years after Independence for flood control, irrigation and power, it holds back a reservoir so large it looks like an inland sea.

Gandhi Minar and the Jawahar (Nehru) Minar give panoramic views, sunsets are the draw, and migratory birds arrive in winter.

best_time.text: October to February, when winter birds are on the reservoir.

how_to_reach.text: Sambalpur is the nearest station and Jharsuguda the nearest airport; the dam is reached by road from Sambalpur.

places.name: Raghurajpur
places.summary: India's first heritage crafts village — Pattachitra painters, palm-leaf engraving and Gotipua dance, 14 km from Puri.
places.seoDescription: Raghurajpur: India's first heritage crafts village, 14 km from Puri — Pattachitra, palm-leaf engraving, masks and Gotipua; open 9 am–6 pm, free.

overview.text:
Raghurajpur, 14 km from Puri, is India's first heritage crafts village. Almost every household here practises a traditional art: Pattachitra painting above all, with palm-leaf engraving (tala pattachitra), stone carving, wooden toys and masks. House walls are painted with murals from Hindu mythology.

The village is known for Gotipua dance and is the birthplace of the Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra. Walk the lanes, watch artists at work and buy straight from them.

how_to_reach.text: By road from Puri (14 km) or Bhubaneswar. Pipili is 25 km away, so the two make an easy pair.

items.body: Buy crafts directly from the artists.

overview.text:
Pipili, on the Bhubaneswar–Puri highway, is Odisha's appliqué village. Its chandua work — bright cloth cut and stitched into flowers, animals and mythological designs — is used in Jagannath Temple rituals and to decorate the Rath Yatra chariots, and it has GI status.

The main street is lined with shops selling umbrellas, canopies, bags, lampshades and wall hangings, and you can watch artisans stitching.

how_to_reach.text: It sits on the Bhubaneswar–Puri highway (NH-316), an easy stop between the two. Dhauli is 12 km and Raghurajpur 25 km away.

places.name: Mangalajodi
places.summary: Chilika's community-run bird wetland — former poachers now guide boats through winter flocks.
places.seoDescription: Mangalajodi: Chilika backwater wetland, community-led conservation, eye-level birding by country boat; best November–February, 6 am–6 pm.

overview.text:
Mangalajodi is the marshy northern backwater of Chilika Lake and one of India's best examples of community-led conservation: once known for bird poaching, its former hunters now protect the birds and guide visitors.

Every winter thousands of migratory birds arrive, and you see them at eye level from traditional country boats gliding through narrow channels — best at dawn.

items.title: Fees
items.body: No entry fee; boat charges apply

best_time.text: November to February, when the migrants are in.

places.name: Ratnagiri and the Diamond Triangle
places.summary: Odisha's Buddhist Diamond Triangle — Ratnagiri's monastery and stupas, with Udayagiri and Lalitagiri nearby.
places.seoTitle: Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitagiri — Odisha's Diamond Triangle
places.seoDescription: Ratnagiri: 5th–13th century Buddhist monastery and ASI museum in Jajpur, with Lalitagiri and Udayagiri; open 9 am–5 pm, ₹25 Indians, ₹300 foreigners.

overview.text:
Ratnagiri, in Jajpur district, was a thriving centre of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism between the 5th and 13th centuries CE. Its monastery has richly carved doorways and panels, and the site holds one of India's largest concentrations of votive stupas; an ASI museum displays the finds.

With Udayagiri (10 km) and Lalitagiri (25 km) it forms Odisha's Buddhist Diamond Triangle. Lalitagiri is among the oldest of the three; excavations there uncovered relic caskets.

how_to_reach.text: By road: 30 km from Jajpur Road, 55 km from Cuttack and 100 km from Bhubaneswar, the nearest airport.

items.body: Explore Ratnagiri's monastery ruins and stupas.
Add Udayagiri (10 km) and Lalitagiri (25 km).
See Lalitagiri's site museum (6 am–6 pm).

places.name: Chandrabhaga Beach
places.summary: Konark's sunrise beach — Magha Saptami bathers and the International Sand Art Festival.
places.seoDescription: Chandrabhaga Beach: 3 km from Konark Sun Temple, sunrise views, Magha Saptami and the International Sand Art Festival; open 24 hours, free.

overview.text: Chandrabhaga is the golden beach 3 km from the Konark Sun Temple. It is a place for sunrises, and every year at Magha Saptami (January–February) thousands gather here for the solar festival. It also hosts the International Sand Art Festival.

best_time.text: October to February; come at dawn for the sunrise.

how_to_reach.text: By road via Konark and Puri. Ramachandi beach is 5 km away.

items.body: Walk the beach after visiting Konark.
Time a visit for Magha Saptami or the Sand Art Festival.

items.title: Early risers
items.body: Sunrise over the Bay of Bengal.

items.title: Swim safely
items.body: Only in designated areas with lifeguards; follow the flags; stay out at high tide, in rough seas and during cyclone alerts.
